rv.q: None of this takes away from the full-bodied intensity of the production, which is fantastically original, gripping and magnificent to the end.
Stone’s dialogue crackles with wit, particularly between Edward, his daughters (Gracie Oddie-James and Isobel Akuwudike) and his old friend Lyle (John Macmillan, very funny and frank).
Stone’s 2016 adaptation of Federico García Lorca’s Yerma with Billie Piper was an Olivier-winning triumph; here, his brilliance comes only in waves.
It’s Succession -level skilful moment by moment, but alienatingly relentless en masse.
Stone has lost sight of what this play's actually about.
It is a hugely enjoyable evening, full of insight and provocation.
